faqs.question: What are the opportunities in government sector in Mechanical Engineering?
faqs.answer: Mechanical engineers have significant responsibility in the government sector in India and also towards different structure, defense technology and services. They play a vital role in the nation's development through designing, developing, and maintaining the mechanical systems in industries, organizations, and business entities. Public Works Department (PWD): Mechanical engineers play a major role right from conception of construction projects related to roads bridges buildings and other facilities to the actual construction phase. They also maintain responsibility of such structures as well as their repair works. Indian Railways: The mechanical engineers have specific importance for the Indian Railways since they are involved in the design, construction and management of Locomotives, carriages and railway tracks. They also participate in the provision of new technologies in railways. Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO): Mechanical engineers are meaningfully engaged in DRDO to deal with sophisticated technologies related to missile systems, aircrafts, and combat vehicles. They participate in the engineering of these systems in terms of architecture, development as well as in testing them. Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs): Mechanical engineers are involved in industries like power production in BHEL, manufacturing industry in SAIL and petroleum industry in ONGC, where huge machinery, machines and structures are involved. overview: The Mechanical Engineering admission in India involves both Class 12 merit and entrance exam scores. Mechanical Engineering courses after 12th are intended to teach students about the planning, design, building, and testing of various mechanical equipment, systems, and machinery. There are various Mechanical Engineering specializations for students to pursue, including Robotics Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Thermal Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and Nanotechnology.

The usual Mechanical Engineering admission eligibility criteria for UG courses require students to complete Class 12 in the Science stream with a minimum of 50 to 60 percent marks in PCM subjects. For PG courses, students must hold a bachelor's degree in the same or a related field with at least 55 percent marks. Some of the prominent Mechanical Engineering entrance exams in India for admission to the B Tech Mechanical Engineering course include JEE Main and JEE Advanced, TNEA Counselling, MHT CET, KCET, AP EAMCET, and COMEDK UGET. Further, most admissions to MTech Mechanical Engineering take place on the basis of the GATE scores.

There are more than 6,400 full-time Mechanical Engineering colleges in India, are IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Madras, VIT Vellore, Delhi Technological University (DTU) , BITS Pilani, NIT Surathkal, NIT Trichy, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, and Jadavpur University. The B Tech Mechanical Engineering fees is approximately INR 2 lakh to INR 12 lakh.

Top-ranked colleges in India provide admission to students on the basis of entrance exam marks; but , a good number of private B Tech Mechanical Engineering colleges also give admission based on Class 12 merit. They often take additional assessment rounds, like the Group Discussion or Personal Interview. These colleges are known for their excellent learning environment, practical exposure and, most importantly, placement records.
